entries.text: Star Bazaar
A small company in a shared, indifferent sky.

Everything under this sky is shared, and counted. Every credit goes into the Common Ledger and comes back in portions. The Plan is generous. It is also five cycles long, and then another five.

You run a small trading company. You start with one home world, one ship's worth of cash and a scout that finds other worlds. Ships fly your routes by themselves. You choose where to invest.

Worlds grow when their needs are met. Raise one into a capital and build the Star Bazaar there, stage by stage. Open it with a final delivery before your term ends. Pick one market to lean on: Military, Luxury, Minerals or Biotech. Three houses send weather, not war.

What it costs the sky, the sky does not say.

Musk

entries.text: A garrison has a war to feed

The Admiralty wills Ashgate's high-ring garrison to keep fighting, and Quartermaster Hanno Sulo wills the invoices to match. He bought your first cargo. {bot1} once sent him painted ballast marked as shells. He offers a standing contract with a deposit, or cash by the lot.
Sign the contract
Get: Military volume up a little for a while. Cost: {cash_out} credits as the deposit to the garrison. Weather: {bot1}'s next weather comes a little later.
The contract is signed

Sulo signed with a seal and kept {bot} as a second source, on probation. Orders now come on a schedule and the deposit cost you credits, so Military volume rises for a while. {bot}'s next weather comes a little later. Each crate is read a litany on the dock, and one rattled.
entries.place: MIL_A1 result popup, opt_a; {bot} is bot_1

entries.text: {bot1}: next weather comes a little later.
Sell by the lot
Get: {cash_in} credits now. Cost: Military volume down a little for a few cycles; {bot3}'s next weather lands a little harder. Weather: {bot1}'s next weather lands a little softer.
Sold by the lot

Sulo counted the cargo against the estimate and paid cash at the dock. Your own orders dip for a few cycles while the berth stands empty. {bot3}'s next weather lands a little harder. {bot}, found with its painted ballast, sees its next weather land a little softer.
entries.place: MIL_A1 result popup, opt_b; {bot} is bot_1

entries.text: {bot1}: next weather lands a little softer.
{bot3}: next weather lands a little harder.
Two fleets claim the same stock

Your contract holds. Two fleets, each sworn to a different estimate, order the same stock in one cycle, and the Admiralty wills both served first. {bot3} brokers between them and bills both. {bot1} serves one fleet. Fill orders in dock order, or by contract term.

entries.text: The garrison has its cargo. Two fleets, each sworn to a different estimate, order the same stock in one cycle, and the Admiralty wills both served first. {bot3} brokers between them and bills both. {bot1} serves one fleet. Fill orders in dock order, or by contract term.
entries.place: MIL_A2 choice screen body after opt_b of MIL_A1

entries.text: Fill orders by dock
Get: Military price up a little for a while. Cost: Ship upkeep rises a little for a while. Weather: {bot3}'s next weather comes a little later.
Orders filled by dock

Orders went out in dock order, and each fleet was told the other had waited longer. The bidding lifts Military prices a little for a while, and two sets of berths raise Ship upkeep a little. {bot}, the go-between, is one messenger too many: its next weather comes a little later.
entries.place: MIL_A2 result popup, opt_a; {bot} is bot_3

entries.text: {bot3}: next weather comes a little later.
Fill orders by term
Get: {n} units of tech progress at the Munitions Line. Cost: {cash_out} credits for the stock. Weather: {bot1} {cut}.
Orders filled by term

Orders went out by term. The fleet {bot1} does not serve held better terms. Its engineers left notes, and your engineer Tavi Brask read them to the press. Tech progress came in. {bot}'s client fell behind, so {bot}'s next weather is held back. The stock cost credits.
entries.place: MIL_A2 result popup, opt_b; {bot} is bot_1

entries.text: {bot1}: {cut_std}.
Sulo sells a stolen ledger

Your orders went out in dock order. Sulo, who changed posts and not habits, waits on the dock with a case: {bot1}'s ledger of clients and berths, copied by hand at night, sealed with the Quartermaster-Saint's thumb. He names a price. A ledger is only a list until it is read.

entries.text: Hand it to your buyers

Get: {cash_in} credits; Military volume up a little for a while. Cost: Ship upkeep up a little for a while; {bot3}'s weather lands a little harder. Weather: {bot1}'s next weather lands clearly softer.
The ledger goes to buyers

Your buyers read the ledger aloud and called on every client it listed. Cash came in and orders rose, and the extra hulls raise Ship upkeep a little for a while. {bot}'s next weather lands clearly softer. Sulo sold a second copy to {bot3}, whose weather lands a little harder.
entries.place: MIL_A3 result popup, opt_a; {bot} is bot_1

entries.text: {bot1}: next weather lands clearly softer.
{bot3}: next weather lands a little harder.
Hand it to your workshop
Get: {n} units of tech progress at the Munitions Line. Cost: {cash_out} credits to the quartermaster. Weather: {bot1}'s next weather lands a little softer, and {bot3}'s comes a little later.
The ledger goes to the shop

Your workshop set the ledger's parts and casting notes beside your own. Tech progress came in at the Munitions Line, and Sulo's price cost credits. {bot}'s next weather lands a little softer, and {bot3}, listed too, sends its next weather a little later. Brask thanked the book.
entries.place: MIL_A3 result popup, opt_b; {bot} is bot_1

entries.text: {bot1}: next weather lands a little softer.
{bot3}: next weather comes a little later.
A new admiral orders new sensors

New Admiral Gabe Nuer took the high ring, and the next day came an order: fit his tracking sensors or pay a heavy port fee. Only his cousin's firm sells them, through {bot1}'s berths, in blessed crates. {bot3} had its own sensors ready. Someone wants the whole market.
Report the scheme
Get: {cash_in} credits now. Cost: Ship upkeep rises clearly for a while. Weather: {bot1}'s next weather lands sharply softer.
The scheme is reported

You sent the order, the price list and the cousin's name to the Bureau. It paid an informant's fee and froze half the refit berths for audit. Your ships stand in queues, so Ship upkeep rises for a while. {bot}'s next weather lands sharply softer: the scheme ran on its berths.
entries.place: MIL_B1 result popup, opt_a; {bot} is bot_1

entries.text: {bot1}: next weather lands sharply softer.
Fit the sensors
Get: Military volume up a little for the rest of the run. Cost: {cash_out} credits for the slips. Weather: {bot3}'s next weather comes a little later.
The sensors are fitted

You paid for the sensors and fitted every ship. The admiral's lanes now list you as trusted, so your Military volume rises for the rest of the run. {bot}'s own sensors were turned away, and its next weather comes a little later. The new sensors hum a canticle no list names.
entries.place: MIL_B1 result popup, opt_b; {bot} is bot_3

entries.text: {bot3}: next weather comes a little later.
Inspector Voss queries a relay

Since your report, Inspector Kethra Voss audits every refit, her stamp worn like a sidearm. One relay in your batch bears the serial of a ship scrapped before your time. {bot2}'s parade squadrons carry it too, and {bot1}'s older fleets. Send it for review, or swap it and refile.

The relay went for review. Voss read your forms, then everyone's. {bot}, whose squadrons carry that relay, lost contracts, and its next weather lands a little softer. The cleared stamp lifts Military prices for a while. One route sat in customs, and its trip cost rises a little.

Get: {cash_in} credits for the old part. Cost: Military volume down a little for a few cycles. Weather: {bot1}'s next weather lands a little softer.
The part is swapped

You swapped the relay and refiled. The old part sold for credits, still humming its dead ship's litany. Voss applied the same clause to {bot1}'s older fleets, which stood idle, so {bot}'s next weather lands a little softer. Ships waited, and Military volume dips for a few cycles.
entries.place: MIL_B2 result popup, opt_b; {bot} is bot_1

The relay review is done. Madame Orlenne Vaux, who runs the high-ring Feast of Arms, offers you a place. {bot3} keeps a stand there every year, always crowded. {bot2} holds a gala next door. Buy the main hall for the week, or take the east stand beside {bot3}'s.

The main hall is yours

You bought the hall for the week, and it cost credits. Buyers walked past empty stands to reach yours, so your Military volume rises for a while. {bot} sold from the corridor, and its next weather lands clearly softer. The relic cannon, which fires blanks only, saluted you.

Get: {n} units of tech progress. Cost: {cash_out} credits for the stand. Weather: {bot2}'s next weather lands a little softer, and all three houses' next weather comes a little later.
The east stand

You took the east stand beside {bot3}'s and paid on the day. Two engineers from the next stand talked shop, and tech progress came in. {bot2}, whose gala crowd walked past, gets a little softer weather, and all three houses, {bot} among them, send theirs a little later.

Your week in the main hall brought the fleets to you. A Fleet Office clerk asks you to set the terms of a supply agreement for many cycles, under an estimate that renews itself with the words until victory. Roster deliveries by garrison, or by week. {bot} watches from the door.

Rostered by garrison

Deliveries are rostered by garrison, each with its own price sheet and blessing. Military orders thinned for a while as the rosters were written, and the price of standing orders rose. {bot} had counted on the fleets as its client, and its next weather lands clearly softer.

Get: {cash_in} credits. Cost: Ship upkeep rises clearly for a while. Weather: {bot1}'s next weather lands clearly softer; {bot3}'s lands a little softer.
Rostered by week

Deliveries are rostered by week from your desk, and the fleets are held ready. A large payment arrived, and the clerk stamped the roster. Ships kept ready cost more, so Ship upkeep rises for a while. {bot}'s next weather lands clearly softer, and {bot3}'s lands a little softer.
entries.place: MIL_B4 result popup, opt_b; {bot} is bot_1

entries.text: {bot1}: next weather lands clearly softer.
{bot3}: next weather lands a little softer.
A patron wants every first crate

Madame Ysolde Marr, a patron on Quillon's gallery ring, wants the first crate of each cycle before any other buyer. She says a crate picks its owner by smell. {bot2} supplies her now, and {bot3} keeps a counter on the same ring. Set a first-pick price, or sell one first lot.
Set a first-pick price
Get: Luxury price up a little for a while. Cost: Luxury volume down a little for a while. Weather: {bot2}'s next weather lands a little softer.
The first pick is priced

Madame Marr agreed a first-pick price, and crates now go to the gallery ring before the shelves. Fewer reach the counters, so Luxury volume dips for a while, and prices rise a little. {bot} lost her first look, and its next weather lands a little softer. She sniffed every lid.
entries.place: LUX_A1 result popup, opt_a; {bot} is bot_2

entries.text: {bot2}: next weather lands a little softer.
Sell one first lot
Get: {cash_in} credits now. Cost: Luxury volume down a little for a few cycles; {bot2}'s next weather comes a little sooner. Weather: {bot3}'s next weather lands a little softer.
The first lot is sold

Madame Marr paid for one first lot at the dock, and the cash arrived the same hour. Shelves stood bare for a few cycles. {bot2} supplied her next lot, so its weather comes a little sooner, while {bot} finds its counter on the ring emptier and its weather lands a little softer.
entries.place: LUX_A1 result popup, opt_b; {bot} is bot_3

entries.text: {bot3}: next weather lands a little softer.
{bot2}: next weather comes a little sooner.
A master finisher takes offers

The first pick is priced and the crates go out. Master finisher Oren Vask has left his guild atelier, which called his signature a smudge, and takes offers for a season. {bot2} wants his hands for its own gem room. Hire him, or take his finished pieces on contract.

Get: {n} units of tech progress at the Atelier. Cost: {cash_out} credits in fees. Weather: {bot2}'s next weather comes sharply later.
The finisher joins the atelier

Vask took a bench in your atelier and showed the crew a cut they had not seen. Tech progress came in, and the fees were paid. {bot} had planned his hands for its gem room, and its next weather comes sharply later. His chalk marks are still on the old bench.

entries.text: {bot2}: next weather comes sharply later.

Get: Luxury volume up a little for the rest of the run. Cost: Luxury price down a little for a few cycles. Weather: {bot2} {cut}.
Pieces on contract

Vask's pieces came to you on contract and fill your counters, priced a little low for a few cycles, so Luxury volume rises for the rest of the run. {bot} lost his work and has its next weather held back. The gems carry a hallmark in a hand nobody knows.

entries.text: {bot2}: {cut_std}.

Vask is at your atelier. Lord Ferrin Gale has sent back a whole batch of {bot2}'s work, calling it loud, and asks you to fill the order. He pays a premium for a name, or gives a place on his list for a price a little low. {bot3} keeps a table at his door.

Get: Luxury price up clearly for a while. Cost: {cash_out} credits for the hallmarks. Weather: {bot2}'s next weather lands sharply softer for a few cycles.

You filled the order under your own mark, and Lord Gale paid the premium. The hallmarks cost credits. {bot}, whose batch was sent back, sees its next weather land sharply softer for a few cycles. The returned crates sit in his cellar, unopened, and he has not asked for a receipt.

Get: Luxury volume up a little for a while. Cost: Luxury price down a little for a few cycles. Weather: {bot3}'s next weather lands a little softer.
Filled by list

You filled the order for a place on Lord Gale's list, at a price a little low for a few cycles. His list sends its friends, so your orders rose for a while. {bot}, whose table stood by the door, sees its next weather land a little softer. The list is written in green ink.

entries.text: {bot3}: next weather lands a little softer.
A pavilion books a masked evening

The pavilion on the Quillon ring has booked an Evening of Many Faces, where every guest arrives as someone else, and wants stock: silk, sunmusk, cut glimmers. {bot2} supplies its cellar, and {bot3} waits with samples. Sell the venue its stock, or stock the stalls yourself.
Sell the venue its stock
Get: {cash_in} credits now. Cost: Luxury volume down a little for a while. Weather: {bot2}'s next weather comes a little later.
The venue buys its stock

The venue bought its stock outright and paid on the night. Your own counters ran thin while the crates were gone, so Luxury volume dips for a while. {bot}'s cellar supply lost the date, and its next weather comes a little later. Every mask in the pavilion faced the door.

entries.text: {bot2}: next weather comes a little later.
Stock the stalls yourself
Get: Luxury volume up clearly for a while. Cost: {cash_out} credits for the stalls. Weather: {bot2}'s next weather lands clearly softer.
Your stalls fill the evening

Your stalls stood in the pavilion all evening, and buyers came to them first. Your orders rose for a while, and the stalls cost credits. {bot} found its crates unwanted, and its next weather lands clearly softer. A mask with nothing behind it hung on every pillar.

entries.text: {bot2}: next weather lands clearly softer.

You sold the venue its stock. The next morning the pavilion's guest list, every name and every order, hung on a wall for a day. {bot3} copied it by the hour, and {bot2} denied there was a list. Study the list at your atelier, or sell your copy.

entries.text: Perk
Marek Voss
Idris Kane
Sela Oru
Tamsin Hale

Marek kept ten ships flying on a shoestring and counts every bolt. He distrusts luck. He started his own company because nobody would let him order spare parts in bulk. He runs Minerals on a Tramp: one more lane beats one big hull.

Idris was a broker with a famous smile and a habit of buying lunch for rivals. He reads a price board the way others read faces. He spends freely and sells hard. He sells Luxury from a Dart: quick hops, a light hold, and the buyer still smiling.

Sela flew supply runs through the worst lanes of the rim and still came home. Bad news does not scare her, only an idle ship does. Her plans have a backup, and a backup for the backup. She runs Military on a Bulkhead. The rim taught her to fill the hold.

Tamsin grew up in the docking rings of the Bazaar and knows every clerk by name. Her contracts arrive with friendly paperwork and larger quantities. She is calm, and a little proud of the old place. She trades Biotech from a Skerrit, a hull she knows.

entries.text: More than half of Military now runs through you, and the Bureau has entered the company as supplier of record. The fleets you supply do not fire. They arrive, they are seen, and the quarrel at the border post ends by itself. The terms are posted and the ledgers can be read, which is dull, and works. Nobody in the Commons sleeps better, because nobody knows how close it was. Harrow Combine still runs its foundries, smaller and watching. The garrisons write you short letters that begin with thanks and end with a requisition.
entries.place: End screen body, win Military, good outcome

entries.text: The Lit Gallery
entries.place: End screen heading, win Luxury, good outcome

entries.text: More than half of Luxury moves through you, and the doors are wide. Silk and cut glimmers went where the Plan had never thought to send beauty: the dock mess, the night shift, the school on the ring. Masks that once cost a season's rations were lent at festivals and came back with a stain and a story. Velvet Concord still keeps the grand tables, though fewer people stand at them. The Bureau drafted a form for the allocation of beauty and then, to its credit, left it blank.

entries.text: More than half of Minerals comes through you, and most of it went into ground. Ingot from the smelter, alloy from the deep cuts, plate from the fabric: the next ring of homes stands on them, with floors that do not ring when walked. The crews rotate on a posted schedule. Harrow Combine still cuts, at its own pace, in its own corner. The Bureau counted the new homes and found, to its surprise, that a form existed for them. Under the floors the stone is patient. It always was.
entries.place: End screen body, win Minerals, good outcome

entries.text: The Long Harvest
entries.place: End screen heading, win Biotech, good outcome

entries.text: More than half of Biotech passes through you, and it goes out the door. Bio-gel and gene seed reached the terraces at Tillam, the fields at Ashgate and clinics nobody had thought to supply. A cure went out on plain paper, with no licence number, and was copied by hand in rooms the Bureau never saw. Velvet Concord still sells the fine strains to those who can pay. The Plan took the credit, which is its way. In the culture lab the vats hum at the pace of something with all the time it needs.
entries.place: End screen body, win Biotech, good outcome

entries.text: The Full Racks
entries.place: End screen heading, win Military, bad outcome

entries.text: More than half of Military runs through you, and the fleets answer. Not to the Commons, and not to you exactly. They answer to the order book, and the order book answers to whoever paid last. The Bureau entered you as supplier of record and asked, very quietly, whether copies of the order forms might reach it first. They cannot. A border post has two flags now and one purchase order. You are never at the front. You only stand where the front is paid for. The racks are full and the cores hum. A great many people are armed, and the Plan has not yet decided what to call it.
entries.place: End screen body, win Military, bad outcome

entries.text: The Gilded Cage
entries.place: End screen heading, win Luxury, bad outcome

entries.text: More than half of Luxury is yours, and everyone wants what only you hold. Prices climb the way stairs do in a dream. Buyers who once haggled now wait, and the ones who cannot wait send guards. Your vaults are lit gold and built like a cell. The Bureau entered you as supplier of record and asked, politely, how many locks. Velvet Concord's masks hang in its empty halls. You hold everything the sky finds beautiful, and no one left may touch it unwatched. The cut glimmers hum faintly as you pass, the way glass does before it breaks.
entries.place: End screen body, win Luxury, bad outcome

entries.text: The Strip
entries.place: End screen heading, win Minerals, bad outcome

entries.text: More than half of Minerals comes through you, and the seams are paying for it. Cinderrest and Greywake were cut to the bone, and then to the bone beneath. White dust has reached the lamps of more rocks, and the Bureau lists every one as uninhabited. They are not. The crews work each cut to its rim until it is gone. Ingot, alloy and plate leave in long rows, and the dead worlds spread one cut at a time. Harrow Combine's crews drift off to other rock. The glass in the walls hums once, low, where it stopped being a wall.
entries.place: End screen body, win Minerals, bad outcome

entries.text: The Locked Seed
entries.place: End screen heading, win Biotech, bad outcome

entries.text: More than half of Biotech is yours, and the seed is locked. Gene seed leaves the culture lab under a seal and a ticket for every batch. The terraces at Tillam and the fields at Ashgate grow what you allow, on terms the Bureau calls reasonable. Nothing is withheld in anger. It is withheld by paperwork, which is quieter. Velvet Concord cannot sell what your wall will not let it copy. The vats are clean and the shelves are full. In the lab, something small and patented turns toward the light.
entries.place: End screen body, win Biotech, bad outcome

entries.text: The Ledger Closes
entries.place: End screen heading, no ship left and cash still negative (loss)

entries.text: The company has no ships left, and the cash is still below zero. Each cycle the Bureau took the newest hull to cover the debt, and now the last is gone. Your ships are entered in the Common Ledger, and your name is given a quota that is equal and exactly the size of everyone else's. A clerk reads the closing form aloud and adds that nothing here was ever owed to you. The three rivals go on selling. The sky did not notice.
entries.place: End screen body, no ship left and cash still negative (loss)

entries.text: The Floor of Every Graph
entries.place: End screen heading, player under a tenth of every market (loss)

entries.text: For three cycles running, your company held less than a tenth of every market, and the Bureau has stopped listing you as a competitor. The strongest of the three rivals fills the shelves where yours stood. Your ships still run, and your orders are still taken, politely, at counters that are no longer yours. Nothing cruel was done. A market is a room, and you were not in it.
entries.place: End screen body, player under a tenth of every market for the sweep window (loss)

entries.text: No Market Held
entries.place: End screen heading, window closed with no market held (soft ending)

entries.text: The window closed with no market held. You did not lose. The company is solvent, the ships run, and the Bureau lists you as a participant, a word with no weight. A spread of small shares does not add up to a market. A single market, held all the way, does. The sky has no opinion. It never needed one.
entries.place: End screen body, window closed with no market over half (soft ending)

entries.text: Cycles taken
Final credits
This run is over. Start a new game or go to the main menu.
entries.place: End screen, above the buttons, every ending

entries.text: New game
Main menu
Quit game
The Standing Fleet kept every rival's growth held down to the last cycle. Nobody asked how.
You bought one rival's best client with a handshake and a gift. The guild filed it as courtesy.
The last seam in reach was yours, and the rivals worked the rest. They do not mention it.
The Patent Wall stands. The rivals' vats run slower behind it, and the clerks call that quality control.
The {workshop} never finished a tech. It ran on habit and steady hands.
entries.place: Epilogue 2, no tech done in the win market

entries.text: One tech came out of the {workshop}. It is mentioned in the minutes.
Two techs came out of the {workshop}. The third is still on the board.
All three techs came out of the {workshop}. The board has run out of things to approve.
{bot} lost a tier in Military and has not come back. Its letters are shorter now.
entries.place: Epilogue 3, a rival lost a tier in Military ({bot})

entries.text: {bot} lost a tier in Luxury. Its masks are still worn, by fewer faces.
entries.place: Epilogue 3, a rival lost a tier in Luxury ({bot})

entries.text: {bot} lost a tier in Minerals. Its crews cut the same rock, with less to show.
entries.place: Epilogue 3, a rival lost a tier in Minerals ({bot})

entries.text: {bot} lost a tier in Biotech. Its vats run on, and its clinics ask for less.
entries.place: Epilogue 3, a rival lost a tier in Biotech ({bot})

entries.text: Military ran second, past a quarter of its market. The fleets noticed, and kept your number.
entries.place: Epilogue 4, Military is a second market over a quarter share

entries.text: Luxury ran second, past a quarter of its market. The masks at the gala came from you.
entries.place: Epilogue 4, Luxury is a second market over a quarter share

entries.text: Minerals ran second, past a quarter of its market. The dust remembers you anyway.
entries.place: Epilogue 4, Minerals is a second market over a quarter share

entries.text: Biotech ran second, past a quarter of its market. A vat in a back room has your name on it.
entries.place: Epilogue 4, Biotech is a second market over a quarter share

entries.text: The Unfinished Bazaar
entries.place: End screen heading, term ended before the Bazaar opened (soft ending)

entries.text: The term is over. The Bazaar is not open, and the Bureau has written that down without any word for it. You did not lose. The crew is paid, the ships are docked, and the worlds you grew are still lit. Someone has left a lamp on in the half-built hall. The Plan will start a new five cycles. The people on the stairs go on climbing them. They have time. So do you, if you want it.
entries.place: End screen body, term ended before the Bazaar opened (soft ending)

entries.text: No stage was finished. The ground is marked out, and the crew sits on it to eat.
entries.place: Epilogue, unfinished Bazaar, no stage done

entries.text: One stage stands. Children from the lower rings walk in and out of it.
entries.place: Epilogue, unfinished Bazaar, one stage done

entries.text: Two stages stand. The third is a frame, and in the evening the wind plays it.
entries.place: Epilogue, unfinished Bazaar, two stages done

entries.text: Only the last hall is missing. The roof has a gap, and the stars use it.
entries.place: Epilogue, unfinished Bazaar, three or more stages done

entries.text: {planet} keeps the site and keeps the lamp lit. Its people call it the Bazaar already.
entries.place: Epilogue, unfinished Bazaar, a capital was founded; {planet}

entries.text: At {planet} the lamps stay on past the hour. The Bureau opens a new page for it.
Lights burn on worlds that were dark when you came. Someone walks home along them.
The grey world has a green edge now. A child there asks what the red haze was.
entries.place: Epilogue, win, a dead world was reclaimed

entries.text: The Wing of Holds is full of crates. The Flagship sits low at its dock.
The Wing of Reach has a long window. From it, other systems look close.
The Wing of Tolls keeps a long desk and a short queue. Everyone is counted twice.
The Wing of Benches smells of hot metal. The night shift has its own kettle.
The Wing of Lamps has shutters for storms. When a storm comes, they stay open.
The Wing of Couriers has a bell for late arrivals. It rings more than it should.
The Ninth Tally
A weak beacon repeats one tone. Nobody has answered it.

A Commons hauler, split along the spine. Its lights are dark. The bunks are empty and made. A Common Ledger plate is still bolted by the hatch. Cutting into the hold takes the scout's time. The flight log is quick to pull, but then the hold stays sealed.
Cut the hold free
Pull the flight log
The crates carry a depot stamp you know. The seals hold. The scout rides heavy on the way back, and the torch is still warm.
Bright cloth, wrapped tight, a sweet smell in the folds. The scout smells of it all the way back. The empty bunks stay behind you.
Dull grey crates, heavy for their size. Dust on your gloves that will not brush off. The scout is slow on the way back.
Damp sealed tubs, warm to the touch. Something in them shifts once, then stops. You do not look twice.
The log lists every stop and every order. A hand wrote the last line twice. The hold stays sealed, and you leave it there.
The log lists ports, buyers and who paid for what. The last page is a list of names. The hold stays sealed behind you.
The log lists every claim the hauler passed, and what each one held. The hold stays sealed. The scout turns away.
The log lists each stop where the cargo was kept cold, and where it stopped being cold. The hold stays sealed.
The Bureau lists the Ninth Tally as overdue. It will stay on that page.
The relay lamp
A relay light blinks twice, stops, then blinks twice again.

A relay station with one lamp lit. A keeper in a shift coat waves from the glass. The shift form lies half filled. If you carry the keeper out, the form stays blank and the lamp goes dark. If you stand the watch, the scout waits and the keeper stays.
Carry the keeper out
Stand the keeper's watch
The keeper hands you a code strip from the relay shelf. The lamp goes out behind you. The form stays blank.
The keeper presses a little gift into your hand, wrapped in bright cloth. The lamp goes out behind you.
The keeper gives you a rock map, marked in grease pencil. The lamp goes out behind you.
The keeper gives you a jar of seed from a window shelf. It is still damp. The lamp goes out behind you.
You hold the lamp for a shift. The relay log shows who passed and what they carried. The keeper sleeps in a chair.
You hold the lamp for a shift. The relay log shows which ships called, and where they sold well. The keeper sleeps in a chair.
You hold the lamp for a shift. The relay log shows which ships hauled rock, and where they sold it. The keeper sleeps in a chair.
You hold the lamp for a shift. The relay log shows which ships carried cold cargo, and where they sold it. The keeper sleeps in a chair.
The keeper's form is filed under the common good. The Bureau does not ask who filled it in.
The quota drum
A tapping on the open band. Always eleven taps, then a gap.

A steel drum drifts in the dark, stamped with a five-cycle plan nobody finished. It taps against its own tether. Inside, a ledger and a sealed lot. If you open the lot, the Plan loses a line. If you copy the ledger, the lot stays closed.
Open the sealed lot
Copy the ledger
The lot is packed in order, each crate numbered. You count them twice. The Plan is one line short, and no one is there to mind.
Folded cloth between paper sheets, still bright. The paper carries a stamp. You leave the stamp where it is.
Heavy slabs in grey wrap, marked for a claim that was never cut. The drum stops tapping when the lot is out.
Cold trays, a green smell in the seam. The drum taps once more, then goes quiet.
The ledger lists every drop and every handler. You copy it by hand. The lot stays closed behind you.
The ledger lists who was owed a gift and who sent it. You copy the names. The lot stays closed behind you.
The ledger lists each claim and its weight. You copy the pages. The lot stays closed behind you.
The ledger lists which trays came from which shelf, and when. You copy it. The lot stays closed behind you.
The Bureau marks the quota drum as found. It does not mark it as finished.
The empty berth
A docking call, repeated. A calm voice, no reply space.

A small station, lit and clean. Every berth is empty and ready. A voice offers you one. A table is set for a crew of six. You may take the stores in the pantry, or stay for the meal and the talk. Both take the scout's time.
Load the pantry stores
Stay for the meal
Rations in sealed packs, stamped for a depot you know. The voice thanks you for each pack. The table stays set.
Tins of sweet things, bright labels, never opened. The voice thanks you for each tin. The table stays set.
Dry stores and tool kits, still in their grease paper. The voice thanks you for each one. The table stays set.
Jars of culture, a label in neat hand on each. The voice thanks you for each jar. The table stays set.
You eat. The voice tells you the stops on the old patrol line, one by one. No one else sits down.
You eat. The voice tells you who dined here, and what each of them paid for. No one else sits down.
You eat. The voice tells you where the nearest rock was cut, and by whom. No one else sits down.
You eat. The voice tells you what grew in the station's garden, and what went wrong. No one else sits down.
The station keeps its lights on. The Bureau has no form for that.
The proving range
A flat tone, struck on the hour. It stops mid-count.

A test range, long abandoned. Targets hang in a line. A rack of tools sits by the control hut, and a crane arm still holds a crate. You can take the rack, or follow the range book to where the last test was logged.
Strip the tool rack
Follow the range book
Drill heads and clamps, in a rack made for one team. Each carries a mark. You do not read them aloud.
Cutters, bits and a core drill, all heavy and oiled. The crane arm lets go of the crate. It floats away.
The book ends at a bearing. You write it down. The last test was never finished, and the book does not say why.
The book ends at a rock field, with depths in pencil. You copy the page. The crate stays in the crane.
The range is struck from the Plan. The targets are still hanging.
The sealed garden
A soft chime and a faint warm light. The beacon is a window.

A glass hull, fogged from inside. Green behind it, thick and still. A hatch will open for a cut flower, or for a full bag of the garden's seed. Either one means going in. Either one means leaving something behind.
Cut the best blooms
Bag the garden seed
Pale petals the width of a hand, with a scent that stays on your sleeve for days. The beds look bare behind you.
Thick blooms, wet at the stem. Your gloves come out stained. The beds look bare behind you.
Fine seed, sorted by colour, each bag tied with thread. The beds stay green, but no one will cut them now.
Seed in damp paper, each lot tagged by shelf. The beds stay green. The air inside smells close.
The garden is listed as tended. No keeper is named on the page.
The Opening
The last hall is roofed. One crate is sealed and signed, and it waits for the Flagship.
The charter cargo is sealed and signed by every hand that built the hall. The crew lines the dock and no one speaks. Every lamp in the Bazaar is dark. It waits for one crate, carried in by you.
Bring the crate in
The crate goes down the long hall in step. The seal breaks. The lamps come on one row at a time, and no one gives an order.
The crate goes in on a cloth of bright thread. The seal breaks, and a warm scent crosses the hall. The lamps come on.
The crate goes in heavy and slow on a flat cart. The seal breaks with a dull knock. The lamps come on, and the walls hum.
The crate goes in damp and warm. The seal breaks, and the air in the hall turns green and close. The lamps come on.
Voltara's reactors run wild

Night-shift engineer Pavo Quill ran Voltara's reactors past the safe-hours rule. Nothing blew up, so the day shift read the rule as a typo. Energy at Voltara costs less and pays less. The cores hum a note nobody tuned, and nobody wants to ask who is listening.
Grey blight on Tillam's terraces

Grey blight crept up Tillam's terraces overnight and rubs off like ash. The committee ruled it a rumour, since no form reports it, and asked the blight to file one. Food at Tillam costs more and pays more. A Seed Bank lets planet storage hold clearly more against the next one.
Ashgate's harvest comes in heavy

Ashgate's harvest came in heavy, and the Common Ledger counted only half. Food at Ashgate costs less and pays less. The other half sits on the dock, real and uncounted, while a boy sells it by the sack from a handcart. What is not on the form is still food, until it rots.
Voltara's crews go hungry

A cheerful official told Voltara's crews that hunger is a slow phase of a smooth future, and handed out a booklet on chewing. Food at Voltara costs more and pays more. The cut was equal for all. The crews note that equal is not full, and read the booklet twice.
Frost on Tillam

Winter came early to Tillam and the heaters never stop. Energy at Tillam costs more and pays more. Frost grows inside the ducts in patterns no one will explain. Old duct-keeper Brindle leaves it a cup of warm oil each night. The cup is empty by morning.
Ashgate lights every furnace

A plan reached Ashgate this morning, written in a hurry and stamped twice. Every foundry was relit to meet it. Energy at Ashgate costs more and pays more. An old brakeman asked what the rush was. Nobody answered, and the furnaces glared on all night.
Tillam's docks go on strike

Tillam's dock crews walked out over a debt they say is owed. The Bureau asked where the debt lives, and the crews pointed at the main gate. The port is closed for a while, and routes touching Tillam are blocked. Hardy Strains reopens a closed planet a cycle sooner.
Ashgate seals its port

Something turned up in Ashgate's lower docks, and the doctors will only say the port is closed. Routes touching Ashgate are blocked until they say otherwise. The dock cat was seen leaving at speed. Nobody here is a witness. Everybody is a suspect.
Voltara goes dark

A fault in Voltara's grid took the port with it. The planet that lights everyone cannot light its own docks. The port is closed for a while, and routes touching Voltara are blocked. The law says lights on. The emergency says off. A clerk decides, by candle.
A lender walks Tillam's market

A lender's agent, a thin man named Shylo Vane, walked Tillam's market and bought every debt in sight. Sellers panicked, settled up and dumped their stock. Energy at Tillam costs less and pays less for now. A debt is real until someone stops believing in the paper.
Ashgate's foreman says enough

Ashgate foreman Dov Rennick read the numbers, said the shift had made enough, and sent his crew home. Energy at Ashgate costs less and pays less. Enough is a word the Plan does not print. By evening three more foremen had found it, and the furnaces cooled.
Voltara buys before the news

A trader named Wex whispered on Voltara's docks that the far beacons had gone dark. They had not. Buyers bought energy hard anyway, and the lie came true by supper. Energy at Voltara costs more and pays more. Price Whisper shows next cycle's prices, rumour or not.
A family buys Ashgate's food

A family with old credits quietly bought every food contract on Ashgate. Their agent, a polite man named Corvale, asked only that nobody ask why. Food at Ashgate costs more and pays more. The Commons has no form for that question yet. It is writing one.
The inspector's count

Inspector Pell counted Voltara's food stores and found them sufficient, on a form. The market believed the form. Food at Voltara costs less and pays less. The pantries are still bare, now correctly accounted for. The form reads smoothly. That is most of the truth.
Tillam's festival of founders

Tillam declared a festival of founders, and everyone wore a founder's mask. Food at Tillam costs more and pays more. Three committees claim to be the real founders. By midnight nobody can tell who is who, and nobody will take off a mask to clear the tables.
A ship leaves Tillam half empty

A ship left Tillam half empty, bound for a rock nobody has charted. Those who stayed sold spare food to pay for staying. Food at Tillam costs less and pays less. A letter came back, from a Tillam that chose otherwise. No one has answered it. It sits on the sill.
Tillam's weavers down tools

Tillam's silk weavers downed tools over a form that counted their hours twice. Silk at Tillam costs more and pays more. An old weaver says to watch the cricket in the vat, which changes shape when it sees another. Fine Finishing makes a Luxury price rise pay clearly more.
Voltara holds a gala

Voltara's crews hold a gala to celebrate a quota met on paper. Silk at Voltara costs more and pays more. Everyone borrows a sleeve and a mask, and by the second hour the crews look alike. Patron's List counts sales here as clearly more Luxury share.
Fire in Voltara's foundry

A fire swept Voltara's core foundry and left the casting floor black. Logic cores at Voltara cost more and pay more. The report calls it a gentle step toward a better line. Ash settled on the walls in neat rows. Nobody has dared to read them.
Ashgate recalls its tractors

Ashgate recalled its farm tractors to be retrained as safe. Logic cores at Ashgate cost more and pay more. The retrained ones freeze when two foremen give opposite orders. The old ones were told to keep quiet and keep going, and they do. They do not look at you.
A rich seam is logged twice

A survey crew found a rich seam and logged it in two offices, so it is counted twice and sold twice. Ore at Voltara costs less and pays less while the news is fresh. With Smelting, ore orders ignore the size cap, so a cheap week can be a big one.
Voltara's foundry wants rock

Voltara's foundry ordered more rock than the Plan had dreamed of. Ore at Voltara costs more and pays more. Every shortcut the founders took lies under the furnace floor, and the furnace wants more. Prospecting lets routes start at asteroid clusters, where the rock is free.
Energy runs short at Voltara

Voltara's night grid asked for more power than the day shift ever booked. Energy at Voltara is wanted harder for a few cycles and the hunger shows in the price. Whoever lands a load in time sells into it, and a rush order may follow.
Food runs short at Tillam

Tillam's pantries ran lean before the terraces could catch up. Food at Tillam is wanted harder for a few cycles and the hunger shows in the price. A full hold arrives as good news here, and a rush order may follow.
Food runs short at Ashgate
Ashgate's ration clerks counted twice and found the shelves thinner than the form said. Food at Ashgate is wanted harder for a few cycles and the hunger shows in the price. A rush order may follow.
Traffic jams at Tillam
A line of convoys waits outside Tillam's docks for a slot nobody can promise. Lanes that touch Tillam cost more per trip for a few cycles. Ride it out or send the ships elsewhere.
Traffic jams at Voltara
Voltara's dock beacons flicker and every captain waits for the next one to go first. Lanes that touch Voltara cost more per trip for a few cycles. Ride it out or send the ships elsewhere.
Wreckage is circling {planet}
A field of old wrecks circles {planet}. Captain Rusk offers to sweep it for a fee. The Bureau filed the wreckage as unowned, so no one has to move it. Routes from {planet} carry less while it stays.
Pay the fee
Pay the fee. The debris is cleared and routes from {planet} run as before.
Leave the debris
Routes from {planet} carry less while the debris stays. It does not clear itself.
Orbit over {planet} is clear
Rusk's tugs swept the orbit and handed you a receipt. Routes from {planet} carry their full load again. The wreckage went somewhere. Rusk smiled when you asked, so you stopped asking.
Debris stays over {planet}
You left the wreck. Ships from {planet} thread around it in the dark and carry less. The offer stays open. Rusk's tug waits at the edge of the field, patient as a bill.
Shade the sun

Chief engineer Ilya Sorn wants to shade part of the sun. The residents wrote to say no, at length. The shield would change markets on planets you can buy later: some goods get cheaper, profit and energy rise. Planets you own stay as they are.
Build the shield
Planets you can buy later change: some resources drop, profit and energy rise.
Leave the sun alone
Nothing changes. The sun keeps its full light.
The shield is up

The shield is up and the sky is dim. Residents filed their anger in triplicate, by lamp. On planets you can buy later, some goods get cheaper while profit and energy climb. Planets you own are untouched. Sorn will not look up.
The shield stays on paper
The plans went back in a drawer. Residents are relieved and sent no thanks. Nothing changes in any market. Sorn asked what the rush had been. No one answered, and the drawer stayed shut.
Nomads on the asteroids

Nomad families live on the asteroids you could mine. They are not on the Common Ledger, so to the Bureau they do not exist. They count their people by who shares the meal. Evict them and the rock is yours. Or let them stay.
Evict the nomads
The asteroids open for mining. Some nomads turn to piracy, and pirates rise.
Let them stay
The asteroids stay closed to mining. No pirates come of it.
The asteroids are cleared
The nomads left on the next tide and said nothing. The rock is yours to mine. Some did not go far. They keep ships now, and a grudge. Pirates rise. Their tables were left set.
The nomads stay
You let the nomads stay. Their lamps burn on the rock, small and steady. A woman brought the first crew to dock a bowl of something hot. The asteroids stay closed to mining.
Pirates reduce trade
Pirates now work the lanes and fewer cargoes get through. Trade volume falls while they stay. The Bureau opened a file on them. It is thin, like the fleet behind it. Every late ship now has a reason.
Hire a clearance crew
Pay to have the pirates cleared. It costs credits and removes their effect on trade.
An asteroid is approaching

A rock is coming in on a slow path. The Bureau saw it late, as it sees everything. The state can turn it aside for a fee, and says it does so out of love. Refusing is a shorter form. Cask Cellar keeps Luxury stock safe from such a cut.
Pay the state
Cost: payment to the state. Asteroid dealt with. The company gains one expansion point.
Decline
An even chance: company storage is hit, or nothing happens.
The asteroid is deflected
The state turned the rock aside and sent you the receipt. The company gains one expansion point. The asteroid drifts on toward someone else's sky. Nobody on the dock looked up until it was gone.
Event reward: the asteroid is dealt with and the company gains an expansion point.
Company storage destroyed

The asteroid struck {planet}. Your company storage there is gone, and what it held with it. The Bureau entered it as an adjustment to the Common Ledger. Nobody said sorry. Your crew stood where the door used to be.

The asteroid grazed {planet}. Your company storage there is cracked and holds less. The Bureau wrote the word partial. The crack runs up the wall in a straight line. Your crew keep their distance from it.
The asteroid passes
The asteroid passed the system and kept going. Nothing was hit and nothing changes. The Bureau withdrew its warning, but kept the form. For one night your crew slept in their boots.
Tillam's sealed granary

Tillam keeps grain behind a lock only the committee can open. Winter is close and the stores outside are thin. The committee will open it for a company that carries the grain out, and wants an answer today. The queue has not moved since dawn.
Open it to the crowd
Food at Tillam costs less and pays less for a while. Tillam remembers.
Keep the lock shut
Food at Tillam costs more and pays more for a while. Tillam remembers.
Send it to Ashgate
Food at Ashgate costs less and pays less for a while. Ashgate remembers.
The granary opens

The lock gave way. The grain went out by hand, sack to sack, and no one in the line spoke. Food at Tillam costs less and pays less while stores are full. The committee recorded a loan. Nobody asked who owes whom.
The lock stays shut

You said no. The lock stayed on and the queue grew in the cold. Food at Tillam costs more and pays more while it is scarce. A child at the front sat on her bag and watched your ship. Inside the granary, something shifted.
Grain goes to Ashgate

The grain left Tillam by night. The loaders worked without lamps and did not look at you. Food at Ashgate costs less and pays less for a while. The committee at Tillam found the empty shelf and wrote a short, cold note.
Tillam burns bright for you

Tillam remembered the grain. Heaters on every terrace run high, and the committee calls it a gift. Energy at Tillam costs more and pays more for a while. The frost in the ducts has gone quiet, as if it was fed.
Tillam closes its port

The queue that waited in the cold came down to the docks. Tillam's port is closed for a while, and routes touching Tillam are blocked. No one shouts. They stand in rows and watch your ships sit still.
Ashgate returns the favour

Ashgate remembered the grain. The foundries run hot in thanks and the smoke leans toward your ships. Energy at Ashgate costs more and pays more for a while. A foreman left a loaf at the dock. It was still warm.
